title: Understanding — Seal — payload
description: The first party (the joining party) proposes a bilateral MyTerms-style agreement grounded in a passed understanding/exchange; the second party (the host) accepts it, refuses it, or counters with a single alternative (carried as a trust-task-error, not a response — see spec.md Authorization). The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

exchangeId.description: The `id` of the understanding/exchange response this seal is grounded in. Its recorded outcome MUST be "understood". Grounds at most one seal negotiation — see spec.md Authorization, "One negotiation per exchange".

respondsTo.description: Present only on the single follow-up permitted after a counter: the `id` of the understanding/seal request the second party countered. See spec.md Authorization, "Answering a counter", for the conditions a recipient MUST check before accepting this follow-up rather than refusing it with understanding/seal:negotiationExhausted.

Response.title: Understanding — Seal — response payload
Response.description: The second party's acceptance of the request named by taskContext, bound by taskDigestMultibase per SPEC §4.9.3 and §7.3 item 20.5's first binding form, so this response can serve as this specification's declared outcome evidence (see spec.md front matter, outcomeEvidence). A counter is carried as trust-task-error understanding/seal:countered, never this shape — this response type means acceptance and nothing else. A refusal uses trust-task-error understanding/seal:refused.

taskContext.description: The `id` of the understanding/seal request this response accepts — the initiating document of this exchange per SPEC §4.9.1. This is the original proposal unless a counter was answered, in which case it is the follow-up request that re-proposed the countered terms.

taskDigestMultibase.description: The task digest of the request named by `taskContext`, computed per SPEC §4.9.3 as multibase(multihash(H(JCS(document ∖ proof)))) over the FULL request document — not merely its `agreement` member — so the binding also covers `exchangeId` and, where present, `respondsTo`.
